meaning.en: To hold one's head high with brows unknit; to feel proud and free of worry or humiliation.
meaning.zh: 抬起头，舒展眉头，形容扬眉吐气、神态得意舒畅。

examples.zh: 比赛夺冠后，球员们仰首伸眉，终于一吐多年的怨气。
examples.en: After winning the title the players held their heads high, shedding years of frustration.

examples.zh: 还清债务后，他终于能仰首伸眉地做人了。
examples.en: Having paid off his debts, he could finally face the world with his head held high.

examples.zh: 受尽冷落的小镇，如今仰首伸眉，成了旅游热点。
examples.en: The long-neglected town now holds its head high as a tourist hotspot.

usage.en: Literary; describes pride and relief after hardship, close to 扬眉吐气. Rare in speech.
usage.zh: 书面语，形容摆脱压抑后得意舒畅，近于“扬眉吐气”，口语少用。

natural: claim credit and demand a reward

meaning.en: To claim credit for oneself, especially undeserved credit, and ask for a reward.
meaning.zh: 把别人的功劳或不大的功劳说成自己的，向上级要求奖赏。

equivalents: take the credit and ask for a reward

examples.zh: 他总是在老板面前邀功请赏，实际干活的却是同事。
examples.en: He always seeks credit in front of the boss, though colleagues do the real work.

examples.zh: 真正做事的人不会四处邀功请赏。
examples.en: People who truly get things done don't go around fishing for rewards.

examples.zh: 项目刚有点起色，就有人跑来邀功请赏。
examples.en: The project had barely improved when someone rushed in to claim the credit.

usage.en: Derogatory; predicate. Suggests exaggeration or stealing credit.
usage.zh: 贬义，多作谓语，含夸大或抢功之意。

meaning.en: Medicines and treatments have no effect; the illness is beyond cure.
meaning.zh: 各种药物和治疗都没有效果，形容病情严重，无法医治。

examples.zh: 老人病情恶化，药石罔效，终告不治。
examples.en: The old man's condition worsened, no treatment helped and he passed away.

examples.zh: 他积劳成疾，最后药石罔效。
examples.en: He worked himself ill and in the end no medicine could save him.

examples.zh: 这种顽疾几乎药石罔效。
examples.en: This chronic illness is almost impervious to treatment.

usage.en: Formal, sombre; used in obituaries and news about serious illness. 罔 means 'no', read wǎng. Also used figuratively of hopeless problems.
usage.zh: 正式、沉重，多见于讣告和重病报道，“罔”意为“无”，读 wǎng，也可比喻无法挽救的问题。

literal: countryside · no · left behind · worthy people

meaning.en: No worthy person is left in obscurity; all the capable have been brought into office.
meaning.zh: 民间没有被遗漏的贤才，形容朝廷选拔人才周全，政治清明。

examples.zh: 古人称赞盛世，常说朝廷之上野无遗贤。
examples.en: In praising golden ages, the ancients often said no worthy person was left out of office.

examples.zh: 公司做到野无遗贤，人人都能得到施展才华的机会。
examples.en: The company leaves no talent untapped; everyone gets a chance to shine.

examples.zh: 要想野无遗贤，选拔制度必须公正透明。
examples.en: To leave no talent overlooked, the selection system must be fair and transparent.

story.en: The Counsels of Yu describe a well-ruled age: 'no worthy person left in the wilds, and the myriad states all at peace' (野无遗贤，万邦咸宁).
story.zh: 《尚书·大禹谟》：“野无遗贤，万邦咸宁。”

date.zh: 东晋 · 约4世纪初（伪古文《尚书》篇章）
date.en: Eastern Jin, early 4th c. (spurious “Old Text” chapter of the Book of Documents)

usage.en: Formal and slightly idealised; used in praise of good government or hiring. Often with 朝无废事.
usage.zh: 正式，略带理想化，多用于称颂政治清明或用人得当。

meaning.en: One shout brings a hundred replies of 'yes': describes great power or status with many followers ready to obey.
meaning.zh: 一声呼唤，百人应答，形容权势极大，前呼后拥，随从众多。

examples.zh: 昔日他在公司一呼百诺，如今却无人理睬。
examples.en: He once commanded instant obedience at the firm; now nobody listens.

examples.zh: 这位帮主一呼百诺，手下数千人听令。
examples.en: The gang boss's one call brings a hundred answers; thousands follow his orders.

examples.zh: 当了领导，他享受着一呼百诺的感觉。
examples.en: Once in charge, he enjoyed the feeling of everyone jumping at his word.

usage.en: Mostly used of influence, with a slight edge of sarcasm if used of a boss. Compare 一呼百应 (many respond to a call, positive and about popular support).
usage.zh: 多指权势，对领导用时略带讽意。与“一呼百应”不同，后者多指号召力强、响应者多。

meaning.en: To level completely, so that nothing is left standing.
meaning.zh: 把建筑物等彻底铲平或摧毁，变成平地。

examples.zh: 地震将整个村庄夷为平地。
examples.en: The earthquake flattened the entire village.

examples.zh: 战火把古城夷为平地。
examples.en: War razed the ancient city to the ground.

examples.zh: 老旧厂房被夷为平地，准备建成公园。
examples.en: The old factory was levelled to make way for a park.

usage.en: Usually passive (被夷为平地) or with 把. 夷 means 'to level', read yí.
usage.zh: 常用“被夷为平地”或“把……夷为平地”。“夷”意为铲平，读 yí。

meaning.en: To lose a critical opportunity through delay or error, originally in battle.
meaning.zh: 因拖延或失误而错过作战的有利时机，也泛指耽误关键时机。

examples.zh: 指挥官犹豫不决，贻误战机。
examples.en: The commander hesitated and missed the decisive moment.

examples.zh: 审批拖拖拉拉，贻误战机，项目被对手抢走。
examples.en: Approval dragged on, the chance was lost and a rival took the project.

examples.zh: 防汛关键时刻不能贻误战机。
examples.en: One must not waste the critical moment during flood control.

usage.en: Formal; predicate. Also used figuratively in business and emergency response. 贻 is read yí.
usage.zh: 正式，多作谓语，也比喻商业、救灾等关键时机。“贻”读 yí。

meaning.en: Many doubts and suspicions arise at once.
meaning.zh: 疑点很多，一个接一个地冒出来。

examples.zh: 这份财务报告前后矛盾，让人疑窦丛生。
examples.en: The financial report contradicts itself and doubts keep arising.

examples.zh: 听了他的解释，大家反而疑窦丛生。
examples.en: His explanation only raised more doubts.

examples.zh: 案情疑窦丛生，警方决定重新调查。
examples.en: The case was full of doubts, so the police decided to reinvestigate.

usage.en: Formal; predicate. 窦 originally means 'hole', so 疑窦 = 'point of doubt'. Compare 疑云重重.
usage.zh: 正式，多作谓语。“窦”本指孔洞，“疑窦”即疑点。

meaning.en: To dedicate one's life to one's country.
meaning.zh: 把自己的一生献给国家。

equivalents: devote one's life to one's country
pledge one's life to the nation

examples.zh: 他立志以身许国，毅然投笔从戎。
examples.en: He vowed to give his life to the country and resolutely joined the army.

examples.zh: 这位科学家以身许国，隐姓埋名数十年。
examples.en: The scientist devoted himself to the nation, living under a false name for decades.

examples.zh: 烈士以身许国，青春永远定格在战场。
examples.en: The martyr gave his life for the country and his youth remains forever on the battlefield.

usage.en: Solemn; praise. Note 身 reads shēn (the chunk's pinyin was wrong).
usage.zh: 庄重，褒义。“身”读 shēn。

natural: look at the sky through a tube

meaning.en: To look at the sky through a tube: to see only a tiny part and so judge narrowly.
meaning.zh: 从竹管里看天，比喻见识狭窄、片面。

equivalents: see only a sliver of the whole

examples.zh: 仅凭一两个例子下结论，不过是以管窥天。
examples.en: Drawing conclusions from just one or two examples is looking at the sky through a tube.

examples.zh: 读书太少，难免以管窥天。
examples.en: With so little reading, one is bound to see too little.

examples.zh: 不要以管窥天，看问题要全面。
examples.en: Don't take such a narrow view; look at the whole picture.

story.en: Zhuangzi mocks those who 'peek at the sky through a tube and point at the earth with an awl — is that not small?' (用管窥天，用锥指地，不亦小乎).
story.zh: 《庄子·秋水》：“用管窥天，用锥指地，不亦小乎？”

date.zh: 战国中期 · 前4—前3世纪

usage.en: Derogatory, often used humbly of one's own view (以管窥天，见笑了). Similar to 管中窥豹 and 坐井观天.
usage.zh: 贬义，也常自谦用，如“以管窥天，见笑了”。近于“管中窥豹”“坐井观天”。

meaning.en: The real meaning lies beyond what is said; the words imply more than they state.
meaning.zh: 真正的意思不在话语表面，而在话语之外，让人自己体会。

examples.zh: 他这番话意在言外，大家都听出了弦外之音。
examples.en: His remark meant more than it said, and everybody heard the hint.

examples.zh: 这首诗意在言外，需要细细品味。
examples.en: This poem means more than its words; it needs careful savouring.

examples.zh: 领导只说“再看看”，其实意在言外。
examples.en: The boss merely said 'let's see', but he meant more than that.

usage.en: Neutral; predicate. Compare 言外之意 (noun, 'implication') and 弦外之音.
usage.zh: 中性，多作谓语。可与“言外之意”“弦外之音”比较。

meaning.en: To get something done thanks to other people's efforts rather than one's own.
meaning.zh: 依靠别人的力量才把事情办成，自己没有真本事。

examples.zh: 他的成绩全靠组员，不过是因人成事。
examples.en: His results all came from the team; he merely succeeded through others.

examples.zh: 要想有真本事，就不能总想着因人成事。
examples.en: If you want real skill, don't always rely on others to get things done.

examples.zh: 别人说我因人成事，我无话可说。
examples.en: They say I only succeeded through others and I can't argue.

story.en: When Mao Sui shamed the other retainers, he said they were 'ordinary people who get things done by relying on others' (公等录录，所谓因人成事者也).
story.zh: 毛遂对同行门客说：“公等录录，所谓因人成事者也。”

usage.en: Mildly derogatory; often a mocking verdict. Not 'making use of people skilfully', which would be 知人善任.
usage.zh: 略带贬义，多用于讥评，不是善于用人。

natural: lure the snake from its hole

meaning.en: To lure a hidden enemy or wrongdoer into the open so as to catch or deal with them.
meaning.zh: 设法诱使隐藏的对手或坏人暴露出来，以便抓获或处置。

examples.zh: 警方设下圈套，引蛇出洞，抓获了诈骗团伙。
examples.en: The police set a trap to flush the gang out and caught the fraudsters.

examples.zh: 他们故意放出假消息，想引蛇出洞。
examples.en: They leaked false news on purpose to flush the culprit out.

examples.zh: 这场测试只是引蛇出洞，真正的审查还在后面。
examples.en: This test is merely bait; the real inspection is yet to come.

usage.en: Neutral; common in crime reporting and politics. Can also be sinister when used of luring dissenters.
usage.zh: 中性，常见于案件报道和政治语境，用于诱使异见者暴露时则带阴险色彩。

meaning.en: To crane the neck and gaze into the distance, expressing eager expectation or longing.
meaning.zh: 伸长脖子远望，形容殷切盼望。

examples.zh: 村民们引领而望，期待亲人早日归来。
examples.en: The villagers craned their necks in the hope their loved ones would return soon.

examples.zh: 全国球迷引领而望，等待决赛开始。
examples.en: Fans across the country eagerly awaited the final.

examples.zh: 老母亲每天在村口引领而望。
examples.en: The old mother gazes down the road from the village entrance every day.

usage.en: Literary; 领 here means 'neck'. Also appears as 引颈而望.
usage.zh: 书面，“领”指脖子。也作“引颈而望”。

meaning.en: To advance with courage and diligence, never slackening in one's pursuit.
meaning.zh: 勇敢无畏、不懈努力地前进。

examples.zh: 他练功勇猛精进，几年便成了行家。
examples.en: He trained with such determination that within a few years he was an expert.

examples.zh: 创业者需要勇猛精进的精神。
examples.en: Entrepreneurs need the spirit of fearless advance.

examples.zh: 面对新技术，团队勇猛精进，很快赶了上来。
examples.en: Faced with new technology, the team pressed on and quickly caught up.

usage.en: Formal; praise. Of Buddhist origin: 精进 is the virtue of diligence (vīrya). Often used of study, practice and careers.
usage.zh: 正式，褒义。源自佛教，“精进”指勤奋不懈，常用于修行、学习和事业。

meaning.en: To be so charmed that one's mind drifts off in longing and admiration.
meaning.zh: 神情悠闲，内心被深深吸引，非常向往。

examples.zh: 听着老人讲草原的故事，我悠然神往。
examples.en: Listening to the old man's tales of the grasslands, I was lost in longing.

examples.zh: 看到山水画，他不禁悠然神往。
examples.en: Seeing the landscape painting, he could not help dreaming of such places.

examples.zh: 她望着海报上的雪山，悠然神往。
examples.en: She gazed at the snow mountains on the poster, entranced.

usage.en: Literary; predicate or adverbial. Often followed by 的 clause on the thing admired.
usage.zh: 书面，多作谓语、状语。

natural: let eyes and heart roam free

meaning.en: To look freely over the scenery and let one's feelings range widely.
meaning.zh: 放眼纵览，舒展心怀，形容尽情欣赏景色、抒发情怀。

equivalents: gaze out and let the mind roam

examples.zh: 登上山顶，游目骋怀，心胸顿觉开阔。
examples.en: On the summit one surveys the view and feels the spirit widen.

examples.zh: 假日里，他喜欢在湖边游目骋怀。
examples.en: On holidays he likes to gaze over the lake and let his thoughts wander.

examples.zh: 站在海边游目骋怀，烦恼一扫而空。
examples.en: Standing by the sea, taking in the view, his worries vanished.

story.en: Wang Xizhi: 'To let the eyes roam and the heart gallop is enough to exhaust the pleasures of sight and sound' (所以游目骋怀，足以极视听之娱).
story.zh: 王羲之《兰亭集序》：“所以游目骋怀，足以极视听之娱。”

usage.en: Literary; often used of enjoying nature. 骋 means 'gallop', read chěng.
usage.zh: 书面，多形容欣赏自然风光。“骋”读 chěng。

meaning.en: Wavering and unable to settle on a position or decision.
meaning.zh: 摇摆不定，拿不定主意或立场不稳定。

examples.zh: 他对去留问题游移不定。
examples.en: He wavers over whether to stay or go.

examples.zh: 投资者态度游移不定，股市随之震荡。
examples.en: Investors are wavering and the market swings with them.

examples.zh: 她的眼神游移不定，显然心里有事。
examples.en: Her gaze kept shifting; clearly something was on her mind.

usage.en: Predicate; also used of eyes or attitudes. Close to 摇摆不定 but a bit more written.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，也可形容目光、态度，比“摇摆不定”略书面。

natural: fated to meet but not to be together

meaning.en: To be fated to meet but not to be together; used of relationships that cannot work out.
meaning.zh: 有相遇的缘，却没有相守的福分，多指恋人或朋友终究不能在一起。

equivalents: meant to meet but not to be

examples.zh: 他们彼此倾心，却有缘无分。
examples.en: They loved each other but were not destined to be together.

examples.zh: 和那所大学有缘无分，我最终去了另一所。
examples.en: It wasn't meant to be with that university, and I ended up at another.

examples.zh: 可惜我们有缘无分，只能各奔东西。
examples.en: Sadly it was not to be; we each had to go our own way.

usage.en: Mostly romantic regret, but can be used lightly of jobs or chances. 分 is read fèn ('lot').
usage.zh: 多用于感情遗憾，也可轻松用于工作、机会。“分”读 fèn。

meaning.en: To be improper and undignified, especially for one's status.
meaning.zh: 不合乎规矩或身份，行为不得体。

examples.zh: 在正式场合穿拖鞋，未免有失体统。
examples.en: Wearing slippers on a formal occasion is rather improper.

examples.zh: 身为教师，在课堂上大发脾气有失体统。
examples.en: For a teacher to lose his temper in class is unbecoming.

examples.zh: 两位代表当众争吵，有失体统。
examples.en: The two delegates quarrelled in public, which was undignified.

usage.en: Formal; used as a criticism of behaviour that is unbecoming to one's role. Compare 有伤大雅.
usage.zh: 正式，批评行为与身份不符。可比“有伤大雅”。

meaning.en: Not yet fully fledged: still young, immature or not strong enough to act independently.
meaning.zh: 鸟的羽毛还没有长齐，比喻年纪轻、力量弱，还不成熟。

examples.zh: 这家创业公司羽毛未丰，还经不起大风浪。
examples.en: The start-up is not yet fledged and cannot weather big storms.

examples.zh: 他羽毛未丰，却想挑战行业巨头。
examples.en: He is still green but wants to challenge the industry giants.

examples.zh: 孩子羽毛未丰，还需要父母多指点。
examples.en: The child is not yet fully fledged and needs more guidance from his parents.

usage.en: Neutral; used of people, firms or forces. Often in 羽毛未丰，不宜…. The form 羽翼未丰 is more common in some usage.
usage.zh: 中性，可用于人、企业或势力。“羽翼未丰”也很常用。
